name: LLM-Based Agents for Tool Learning: A Survey (Xu et al.)
venue: Data Science and Engineering (Springer), Volume 10, pages 533-563, published 26 June 2025; open access; DBLP journals/dase/XuHGS25
authors_affiliation: Weikai Xu, Chengrui Huang, Shen Gao, Shuo Shang. All authors: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC), Chengdu, China.
code_url: N/A (no official code/maintained paper-list repository is referenced by this survey; the only GitHub reference inside the paper is to the cited method GitAgent, not the survey itself)
maintained_repo_url: N/A (the survey does not maintain a continuously-updated GitHub paper list or leaderboard)
task_domain: tool-use (tool learning by LLM-based agents): the survey covers tool invocation timing, tool retrieval/selection, tool planning, multimodal tools, downstream applications (data science, software engineering, web/mobile, robotics), benchmarks/metrics, and safety/ethics.
problem_setting: Survey/taxonomy of LLM-based tool-learning agents. The problem is framed via the 'Three Ws': Whether to invoke a tool, Which tool(s) to retrieve, and HoW to use them. Settings span single-agent and multi-agent frameworks, interactive (environment-feedback / reflection loops) and offline-trained pipelines, with both training-based (supervised fine-tuning on open-source LLMs) and non-training (in-context / prompting on closed-source LLMs such as GPT-4) approaches. A canonical agent framework is defined with five components (executor, perceiver, validator, controller, retriever) operating iteratively over a toolset and environment until subtasks are resolved.
what_is_retrieved: tools / APIs (and their documentation: tool background knowledge + query-tool-invocation-response demonstration triplets). Secondarily, demonstrations/exemplars for in-context tool use are retrieved for non-fine-tuned LLMs.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus of user-defined tools/APIs (e.g., RapidAPI hub, HuggingFace/TensorFlow/Torch Hub model APIs, RESTful APIs). The survey notes tool documentation grows outdated and discusses methods to integrate new tools, but the dominant grounding is a static/user-defined tool repository rather than agent-written growing memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Mixed/both. The survey describes top-k structured retrieval (greedy/staged search, rerank-then-truncate) and emphasizes cross-category then in-category comparative screening to recover the correct (possibly multiple) tools for multi-tool tasks; it discusses one-to-many API mapping where Recall (completeness of the needed set) matters beyond single-instance accuracy.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (the survey is not framed as case-based reasoning; closest analogs are demonstration retrieval and reflection-driven revision, but no explicit Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain CBR cycle is invoked) [uncertain]
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The survey does not frame tool learning as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; reflection and demonstration reuse are discussed under their own terminology.
retrieval_unit: tool-API (the primary retrievable unit), together with tool documentation (background description + demonstration triplets). For non-trained LLMs, single demonstrations/exemplars are also retrieved. ToolkenGPT treats tools as special tokens ('toolkens') predicted in the generation stream (tool-as-token granularity).
index_source: Static external tool corpora: virtual API servers (StableToolBench cache+simulator) and real APIs (RapidAPI hub with 16k+ APIs, HuggingFace/TensorFlow/Torch Hub, RESTful services, OpenAI plugin lists). The survey notes documentation can become outdated and discusses auto-integration of new tools, but the store is predominantly offline/user-defined rather than agent-grown.
index_structure_topology: Mostly hierarchical/category-keyed: ToolLLM structures RapidAPI into hierarchical tree (coarse-grained category -> fine-grained sub-category -> tool/API) enabling tree-search retrieval (DFSDT, MCTS). Flat dense vector indices are also used (dual-encoder retrievers). Tool dependency / invocation-sequence structures are noted (ToolChain* stores invocation sequences).
retriever_type: Hybrid across the surveyed works: dense dual-encoder retrievers, classification/generative tool prediction (ToolkenGPT tool-as-token via toolken embeddings), tree/graph search-based retrieval (DFSDT, MCTS, A* in ToolChain*), and LLM-as-retriever/selector via prompting (AutoGPT, HuggingGPT). Cross-encoder rerankers are used downstream (ToolRerank).
retriever_learning_signal: Multiple, organized by the survey's training-based vs non-training-based split: (1) none / off-the-shelf in-context (closed-source LLMs prompted with documentation+demonstrations); (2) supervised fine-tuning with coarse/fine-grained classification + API classification losses (ToolLLM); (3) curriculum / introspective-feedback iterative data construction (Confucius ISIF, easy-to-difficult); (4) self-play / data-augmentation bootstrapping (TALM); (5) knowledge distillation from teacher LLMs (ToRA); (6) toolken-embedding training on contextual examples (ToolkenGPT).
query_construction: Intent extraction from the user command (intent distribution model / semantic analysis), then task decomposition into subtasks; each subtask becomes a structured retrieval query within the toolset. Documentation may be expanded/standardized (EASYTOOL compression) and retrieved API docs are concatenated into the prompt (Gorilla) to condition subsequent reasoning.
query_granularity: Both task-level and subtask/step-level: the controller decomposes the user query into multi-step subtasks, and retrieval is performed per subtask (one tool per subtask in the ideal decomposition), so queries are constructed at trajectory/step granularity over the iterative loop.
when_to_retrieve: Both one-shot and iterative depending on the method. The canonical framework is iterative: the controller/retriever progressively narrows the candidate tool pool over rounds based on perceiver feedback and validator reflection until all subtasks are resolved. The 'Whether' (tool invocation timing) decision governs whether retrieval is triggered at all.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Tool-invocation necessity judgment ('Whether'): Toolformer's criterion is whether the model can answer correctly without a tool; AnyTool/Du extends this to first check whether the current toolset even contains a useful tool, weighing invocation cost vs task-resolution efficiency. In the iterative framework, the controller re-triggers retrieval based on perceiver feedback and validator reflection (agent-initiated, feedback-conditioned).
reranking: Yes. ToolRerank (ToolReranker) performs adaptive and hierarchy-aware reranking: a dual-encoder retriever produces coarse-grained candidates, Adaptive Truncation cuts the list, then a cross-encoder reranker reranks the truncated set; it is reported to outperform ToolLLM in search efficiency by avoiding multi-round feedback evaluation. Functional reranking by the controller is also noted.
retrieved_context_refinement: Documentation engineering and reranking: EASYTOOL compresses/standardizes heterogeneous tool documentation (addressing inconsistency/redundancy) and auto-fills/validates parameters; rerank-then-truncate (ToolRerank Adaptive Truncation); Hsieh et al. show tool documentation enables zero-shot usage. The survey explicitly catalogs documentation issues: inconsistency, redundancy, incompleteness, impracticality.
tool_document_engineering: Central theme. Tool documentation = (1) background knowledge (functionality + parameter definitions) and (2) demonstration examples (query-invocation-response triplets). Engineering levers surveyed: text compression/standardization (EASYTOOL), retrieved-doc concatenation into prompts (Gorilla), auto-integration of new tools (Hsieh et al.), and toolken-embedding learning (ToolkenGPT). Four documentation pathologies are named: inconsistency, redundancy, incompleteness, impracticality.
index_content_separation: Partially: the hierarchical category->subcategory->tool index (ToolLLM) and coarse-retrieve-then-rerank-then-truncate (ToolRerank) effectively separate a lightweight candidate index from heavier per-tool documentation/invocation loaded on demand; ToolChain* stores invocation sequences for evaluation. Not framed as explicit progressive-disclosure but the pattern is present.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: The survey discusses multiple integration protocols across surveyed works: RapidAPI hub, RESTful APIs (RestGPT/RestBench), HuggingFace model invocation (HuggingGPT), and function/token-level invocation (ToolkenGPT). It flags that static documentation becomes outdated and that real APIs fluctuate (motivating StableToolBench's virtual API server with cache+simulator). MCP is not discussed (predates/outside the 2022.6-2024.5 coverage window). No CRUD auto-sync mechanism is standardized.
tool_dependency_awareness: Yes, acknowledged: the survey stresses inter-tool dependencies and invocation order (e.g., latitude/longitude must be obtained before elevation), and notes cross-category then in-category comparison; ToolChain* stores and compares tool invocation sequences (maximum common subsequence) to capture dependency/ordering, and tree-search planners (ToolLLM DFSDT/MCTS, ToolChain* A*) navigate dependency-laden action spaces.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation (retrieved API documentation concatenated into the prompt, Gorilla; demonstration triplets for in-context tool use), latent-token injection (ToolkenGPT toolken embeddings predicted inline then replaced by invocation results), and as a training signal (fine-tuning on retrieved/augmented tool-use corpora). Retrieved tools are then executed by the executor against the environment with parsed feedback.
planning_integration: Both retrieve-then-plan and plan-then-retrieve, and retrieval embedded inside search loops. Internal planners use decomposition (CoT, ReAct, CoA), selection (CoT-SC, ToT, GoT, ToolChain* tree/A* search), and clustering; external planners formalize tasks for symbolic solvers (LLM+P/PDDL, LLM-DP with BFS, AutoGPT+P) or neural planners. ToolLLM interleaves retrieval with MCTS/DFSDT over the hierarchical API tree.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call / per-subtask within the iterative controller-perceiver-validator-retriever loop; ReAct interleaves reasoning+action per step; CoA fills abstract placeholders with tool calls per reasoning chain. Tree/graph-of-thought methods interleave at the per-thought/per-branch level.
adaptation_mechanism: Reflection-driven revision: unsupervised self-reflection (validator checks parameter filling and return correctness, deletes/updates incorrect tools) and supervised external reflection (a stronger agent evaluates tool-invocation appropriateness as gold). Retrieved demonstrations are otherwise used as verbatim in-context exemplars. Not framed as CBR case adaptation. [uncertain mapping to CBR terminology]
retrieved_item_representation: Surface forms surveyed: raw/standardized tool documentation text (description + demonstration triplets) injected into the prompt; executable API calls / function tokens (ToolkenGPT toolkens; Toolformer <API>...</API> translated calls embedded in text); reasoning chains with abstract placeholders reified by tool outputs (CoA).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Predominantly single tool/API + its documentation (a concrete callable unit) and single demonstrations; ToolkenGPT abstracts tools to special tokens; CoA abstracts to placeholder-and-reify reasoning chains. Not distilled strategies/skills in the experience-memory sense.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Validator/self-reflection (unsupervised and supervised-external) to catch wrong parameters/returns; documentation standardization (EASYTOOL) to reduce noisy/redundant docs; staged curriculum training (Confucius) to distinguish similar tools; and dedicated robustness benchmarks (RoTBench five noise levels: Clean/Slight/Medium/Heavy/Union across tool selection, parameter recognition, content generation; Noisy-ToolBench for ambiguous instructions; InjecAgent for indirect prompt-injection attacks).
memory_type: none / not a memory-centric framework. The surveyed canonical framework keeps an invocation history H_t within the controller loop and uses reflection, but it is not organized as episodic/skill-library/graph long-term memory; the retrievable store is a static tool repository, not an agent-written experience memory.
write_back: False (no general experience write-back to a growing memory). Exceptions noted in cited works: TALM self-play and Confucius ISIF dynamically construct/augment training data; ToRA reintegrates corrected outputs into the training set; GitAgent (cited) autonomously extends its toolset from GitHub. These are training-data/toolset growth, not test-time experience memory.
online_growth: Largely no for the retrievable store at deployment; the survey emphasizes that toolsets and documentation become outdated and discusses auto-integration of new tools (Hsieh et al.) and toolset extension (GitAgent), but the dominant setting is a frozen offline tool corpus. StableToolBench freezes API behavior via a cache+simulator for stable evaluation.
write_back_trigger: never (for experience memory) in the canonical framework. Where data/toolset growth occurs in cited works it is training-time and reflective/iterative: Confucius ISIF updates training data based on model introspective feedback; TALM bootstraps via self-play; ToRA reintegrates after error detection/correction (success-and-failure-aware correction). No standardized per-step/human-validated experience write rule.
failure_experience_usage: Partially via output-space correction at training time: ToRA systematically detects errors in generated tool-invocation outputs and corrects (manual/automatic) them before reintegration, mitigating error propagation; reflection deletes/updates incorrect tools at inference. Failures are corrective signals rather than stored failure cases for retrieval.
memory_evolution_update: delta-update / refine-overwrite at the level of training data and toolset rather than a memory store: Confucius ISIF continuously updates the training dataset; reflection updates/deletes incorrect tool choices; EASYTOOL refines documentation. Not an append-only experience log with dedup/forget dynamics. [uncertain mapping]
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Mixed: many surveyed retrievers are learned (supervised classification-based tool retrieval in ToolLLM, toolken prediction in ToolkenGPT, curriculum-trained Confucius), and tree-search planners (DFSDT/MCTS, ToolChain* A*) use learned/heuristic value evaluation, but a substantial portion is fixed similarity top-k (dense dual-encoder) or prompt-based selection. No RL-as-retrieval-policy (e.g., soft Q-learning M-MDP) is centrally featured; online RL environments are flagged only as future work.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Discussed mainly via multi-agent frameworks where specialized agents (planner/caller/summarizer in Shen et al.; code-writer/executor in MechAgents) collaborate and a stronger agent provides external reflection. This is role-specialized collaboration rather than shared retrievable experience memory across heterogeneous frameworks; cross-framework experience sharing is not a focus.
benchmarks: API-Bank; APIBench (Gorilla, 16,460 instructions); ToolBench/ToolLLM (16,464 RapidAPI APIs); ToolAlpaca (400+ APIs, 3938 instances); RestBench (IMDB, Spotify); UltraTool (2032 tools, 22 domains); ToolTalk (7 plugins, 28 tools, 78 dialogues/178 turns); StableToolBench; ToolEyes (~600 tools, 7 scenarios, 5 dimensions); MLLM-Tool / Tool-LMM (932 model APIs from HuggingFace); RoTBench (5 noise levels); InjecAgent (1054 cases, 17 user + 62 attack tools); Noisy-ToolBench (100 RESTful APIs, 1000 ambiguous instructions); ToolQA (8 fields, easy/hard); MetaTool/TOOLE (390 tools); MenatQA (2853 temporal samples); T-eval; plus general datasets (GSM8K). Safety: AdvBench, ToolSword.
benchmark_family: tool (ToolBench/ToolLLM, StableToolBench, API-Bank, APIBench/Gorilla, ToolAlpaca, RestBench, UltraTool, ToolTalk, ToolEyes, T-eval, MetaTool, ToolQA); multimodal-tool (MLLM-Tool/Tool-LMM); robustness/safety-tool (RoTBench, InjecAgent, Noisy-ToolBench, AdvBench, ToolSword); QA/reasoning auxiliaries (GSM8K, MenatQA).
baselines: N/A as a survey (no single set of methods is run head-to-head). The reviewed/compared method families include: ToolLLM, Confucius, ToolRerank, Gorilla, TALM, ToRA, ToolkenGPT, CoA, Toolformer, HuggingGPT, RestGPT, AutoGPT, EASYTOOL, ToolChain*, AnyTool, ReAct, CoT/CoT-SC, ToT, GoT, LLM+P/LLM-DP/AutoGPT+P, and multi-agent frameworks (Shen et al., MechAgents). Backbone LLMs referenced include GPT-4 / ChatGPT and open-source models.
key_metrics: Pass Rate and Pass Rate* (ToolLLM/ToolBench); Win Rate; Accuracy and Recall (one-to-many API mapping); ROUGE-L and Plan Score (T-eval) and MD Point-Wise (UltraTool, 6 dimensions) for plan quality; AST sub-tree matching and Levenshtein Distance for parameter filling; Correct Selection Rate (CSR, MetaTool); Hallucination Rate (MLLM-Tool). Manual, advanced-model (LLM-as-judge), and objective indicators are all catalogued.
headline_result: N/A (survey contributes a taxonomy, not a single headline metric). The most-cited quantitative anchor it reports is ToolLLM/ToolBench covering 16,464 real RapidAPI APIs with the Pass Rate / Win Rate evaluation protocol that downstream tool-learning benchmarks build on. [uncertain as a single number]
ablations: N/A (survey runs no experiments/ablations of its own). It instead analytically contrasts component choices: training-based vs non-training tool retrieval; greedy vs staged-curriculum search; rerank-then-truncate vs multi-round feedback (ToolRerank reported more search-efficient than ToolLLM); internal vs external (symbolic/neural) planners; single-agent vs multi-agent reflection; virtual vs real toolsets.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes, conceptually. The survey separates metric categories: (1) task completion (Pass Rate, Win Rate, Accuracy, Recall), (2) output quality (plan quality: ROUGE-L/Plan Score/MD Point-Wise; parameter filling: AST matching/Levenshtein), (3) tool selection/invocation (CSR), and (4) robustness/error-handling (Hallucination Rate). Intrinsic selection/retrieval quality (CSR, Recall) is thus distinguished from end-to-end completion.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. Beyond final-outcome Pass/Win Rate, the survey highlights process/intermediate metrics: step-wise Plan Score and ROUGE-L for plan quality, AST/Levenshtein for per-parameter correctness, CSR for tool-selection correctness, and MD Point-Wise scoring across accuracy/completeness/executability/syntactic soundness/structural rationality/efficiency.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Discussed qualitatively: tool-invocation cost vs task efficiency drives the 'Whether-to-invoke' decision (AnyTool/Du); ToolRerank reduces search cost by avoiding multi-round feedback evaluation; StableToolBench cache/simulator reduces real-API cost/instability; documentation redundancy (RapidAPI) inflates token consumption; ToolChain* navigates action space more efficiently with A* search. No standardized cost numbers across works.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Reranked-then-truncated selection is the salient pattern (ToolRerank Adaptive Truncation produces a budget-capped candidate set before cross-encoder reranking). Documentation compression (EASYTOOL) targets prompt-token budgets. The survey notes ToolkenGPT's toolken count scales with toolset size, affecting capacity. No single fixed-k is prescribed; k/budget vary by method. [uncertain on exact k values]
survey_scope_and_axes: Organizing axes: (1) the 'Three Ws' task definition (Whether / Which / HoW); (2) a 5-component agent framework (executor, perceiver, validator, controller, retriever); (3) Learning to Use Tools split into training-based (calculation / translation / retrieval, with greedy/staged/rerank/data-augmentation) vs non-training (in-context / documentation); (4) Tool Planning split into internal (decomposition/selection/clustering) vs external (symbolic/neural) planners; (5) multimodal tools; (6) applications; (7) benchmarks (by task complexity, toolset type, special scenarios) and metrics (4 categories); (8) safety/ethics + future directions. Reference count: 166 references; coverage window for the work-summary tree diagram: 2022.6 to 2024.5.
benchmark_construction_and_size: The survey catalogs construction methods/sizes of others' benchmarks rather than building one: e.g., APIBench 16,460 LLM-generated API instructions; ToolBench 16,464 real RapidAPI APIs with ChatGPT-generated instructions; ToolAlpaca 3938 instances over 400+ APIs (simulated); UltraTool 2032 tools across 22 domains; ToolTalk 78 dialogues/178 turns; InjecAgent 1054 cases; Noisy-ToolBench 100 APIs/1000 expert-written ambiguous instructions; MLLM-Tool 932 filtered model APIs; ToolQA spanning 8 fields. Answer verifiability ranges from LLM-generated-then-human-annotated (API-Bank) to virtual-server-stabilized (StableToolBench).
builds_on: Foundational tool-learning and reasoning works it synthesizes: Toolformer (self-supervised tool-call insertion), ToolLLM/ToolBench (16k+ API retrieval with DFSDT), Gorilla/APIBench, HuggingGPT, RestGPT, ReAct, Chain-of-Thought, Tree/Graph-of-Thoughts, ToolkenGPT, CoA, Confucius, ToolRerank, EASYTOOL, ToolChain*, LLM+P/PDDL planners. It positions itself relative to prior tool-learning surveys (e.g., Qin et al. 'Tool learning with foundation models').
contrasts_with: Prior LLM-agent / tool-learning surveys it complements/distinguishes from: Qin et al. 'Tool learning with foundation models' (ACM CSUR); Xinzhe Li's 'A Review of Prominent Paradigms for LLM-Based Agents: Tool Use, Planning (incl. RAG), and Feedback Learning'; planning surveys (Huang et al. 'Understanding the planning of LLM agents'); multimodal-agent surveys. This survey is distinguished by its 'Three Ws' framing, the explicit five-component agent framework, the training-based vs non-training retrieval dichotomy, and a dedicated benchmarks+metrics compilation.
lineage: Surveys group (anchors group E: tool retrieval, selection, and the benchmark landscape). It is a peer-reviewed (Data Science and Engineering) anchor for the tool-learning / tool-retrieval sub-topic, providing taxonomy and benchmark/metric scaffolding that situates method papers on tool retrieval, reranking, dependency-aware selection, and tool benchmarks.
